summary: The Drizzle EQL migration rewriter (two byte-mirrored copies, used by `stash eql migration --drizzle` and the wizard) no longer emits ADD+DROP+RENAME; it emits only `ADD COLUMN "<col>_encrypted"` and leaves the source column. Any skipped/unverified statement now aborts the CLI with exit 1 and makes the wizard throw. This removes the data-destroying path on populated tables, but introduces new release risk: the rewritten SQL no longer matches the Drizzle schema and snapshot that produced it (the TS schema still declares the source column as encrypted), so applications can silently write EQL ciphertext into the plaintext `text` column while the twin stays NULL, and the documented staged flow later collides with the already-added twin. The wizard now defaults the migrate prompt to Yes after such a rewrite. Separately, the new hard exit is swallowed by `stash init`, which then misdiagnoses it as a drizzle-kit problem and reports EQL as not installed; and the shipped stash-drizzle skill still says the swept repair is data-destroying. Rewriter-level behaviour is extensively unit-tested (not run here); the schema/DB-alignment and init paths have no tests.

behaviour_changes.description: Generated SQL for an in-place ALTER to an EQL domain changes from ADD tmp + DROP source + RENAME tmp->source (column keeps its name, becomes encrypted) to a single ADD COLUMN "<col>_encrypted" with the source column left as plaintext. The rewritten migration no longer realises the schema change the Drizzle schema/snapshot describes.
`stash eql migration --drizzle` now throws CliExit(1) (after writing the install migration) whenever the sweep skips any statement or throws; previously it warned and exited 0.

Wizard post-agent step now throws instead of prompting when any statement is skipped or a directory sweep failed; when files were rewritten it now defaults the `drizzle-kit migrate` prompt to Yes (was No).

New skip reason `target-exists` when `<col>_encrypted` is already declared or staged earlier in the sweep; the in-sweep 'already converted' tracking (encryptedColumns.add) was replaced by stagedTargets.
Dollar-quote detection ignores `$` immediately following an identifier character, so identifiers like `price$$cents` no longer open phantom dollar-quoted bodies that hid later SQL from the sweep.
When the sweep throws, it attaches the partial rewritten/skipped lists to the error; the CLI and wizard report them.
skills/stash-cli/SKILL.md updated to describe the add-only, fail-closed sweep; skills/stash-drizzle/SKILL.md (also shipped) was not updated.

failure_scenarios.title: Add-only rewrite leaves the DB out of step with the Drizzle schema; app writes ciphertext into the plaintext column
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user (or the wizard agent) changes `email: text()` to `email: types.TextSearch('email')` in the Drizzle schema, runs drizzle-kit generate, the sweep rewrites the ALTER, and the user runs drizzle-kit migrate (wizard now defaults this prompt to Yes).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: renderSafeAlter now emits only `ADD COLUMN "email_encrypted"` (rewrite-migrations.ts:845-873) and the sweep only edits *.sql files (line 735), so the drizzle meta snapshot and the TS schema still say `email` is an EQL domain. At base the ADD/DROP/RENAME left `email` with the encrypted type the schema expects. The stack-drizzle codec serialises envelopes with JSON.stringify (codec.ts:67-72), which a `text` column accepts.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Writes through the Drizzle model store EQL envelopes as text in `email` alongside existing plaintext rows, `email_encrypted` stays NULL, and encrypted query operators against `email` fail. Following the stash-drizzle staged flow afterwards (declare `email_encrypted` in TS, generate) produces a second ADD COLUMN that fails because the twin already exists; a backfill keyed on `email` would read a column that now mixes plaintext and ciphertext. Mixed-content columns need manual data repair.

missing_verification: No test or check that the rewritten migration plus drizzle snapshot plus TS schema describe the same database (e.g. drizzle-kit generate after the rewrite yields no diff, or a schema that references `<col>_encrypted`).
No end-to-end test of drizzle-kit migrate followed by an insert through the Drizzle model against the rewritten schema.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Either keep the source schema consistent (rewrite only when the TS schema already declares the twin, otherwise fail closed with instructions to declare `<col>_encrypted` and revert the source column type), or have the CLI/wizard stop before migrate and tell the user to edit the schema so the snapshot matches. Do not default the wizard migrate prompt to Yes after a rewrite until this is resolved.

failure_scenarios.title: `stash init` (Drizzle) misreports a fail-closed sweep as a drizzle-kit failure and says EQL is not installed
failure_scenarios.trigger: `stash init` with Drizzle in a project whose migration directory has any ALTER-to-EQL statement the sweep skips (source declared elsewhere, hand-written USING, existing twin).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: generateDrizzleEqlMigration now throws CliExit(1) after writing the install migration (migration.ts:338-343). install-eql.ts:126-143 catches every error, logs 'Could not generate the EQL migration — check that drizzle-kit is installed and configured', and returns eqlMigrationPending unset; init/index.ts:149-160 then prints 'EQL extension NOT installed', tells the user to run `stash eql install`, and exits 1. Co-change history shows migration.ts usually changes with install paths, and this caller was not updated.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Onboarding fails with the wrong diagnosis and a remedy that points away from the real problem (sibling migrations needing review); an install migration file is left on disk while init reports nothing was generated, so a retry can add a second install migration.

failure_scenarios.title: Shipped stash-drizzle skill still describes the swept repair as data-destroying and sends users to a staged flow that collides with it
failure_scenarios.trigger: A customer's coding agent reads the installed stash-drizzle skill after this release.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: skills/stash-drizzle/SKILL.md:64 (head) says the sweep's repair is data-destroying and safe only on empty tables and directs live tables to the staged flow at :450-461, which tells the agent to add `email_encrypted` in the TS schema and generate an ADD COLUMN. The rewriter now already adds that column. The history signal shows migration.ts usually co-changes with this skill.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Agents give wrong guidance in customer repos: they avoid or hand-edit a migration that is now non-destructive, or apply it and then generate a duplicate ADD COLUMN that fails at migrate time.

failure_scenarios.consequence: Loud but persistent: CI scripts or onboarding flows that call the command fail every time; users must edit already-applied migration files to proceed.
